name: Nabal
bio:
Nabal was a man of the clan of Caleb, living in Maon with property at Carmel, very wealthy with three thousand sheep and a thousand goats, but harsh and evil in his dealings. His wife Abigail, by contrast, was intelligent and beautiful (1 Samuel 25:2-3).

While in the wilderness, David had protected Nabal's shepherds and flocks without taking anything; when Nabal was shearing sheep, David sent ten young men asking, in David's name, for whatever provisions Nabal could spare, given the past kindness shown. Nabal answered arrogantly, "Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants are breaking away from their masters these days... Why should I take my bread and water, and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give it to men coming from who knows where?" (1 Samuel 25:4-11). Furious, David set out with four hundred men, vowing to wipe out every male in Nabal's household (1 Samuel 25:12-13, 21-22).

Nabal's wife Abigail learned of this and hurried to intercept David with a large gift, apologizing on her husband's behalf and defusing the bloodshed (1 Samuel 25:18-35). When she returned home, she found Nabal holding a feast, drunk, so she waited until morning, sober, to tell him what had happened; Nabal's heart failed within him, and he became like stone. About ten days later, the LORD struck him down and he died (1 Samuel 25:36-38). On hearing the news, David said, "Praise be to the LORD, who has upheld my cause... and has kept his servant from doing wrong and has brought Nabal's wrongdoing down on his own head," and soon sent for Abigail to become his wife (1 Samuel 25:39). Nabal's very name means "fool" in Hebrew — a fitting match for his stubborn, ungrateful character.
